title: Increasing response scales kept 22 of 26 pollutant interaction signs in fixed invertebrate means from a 2024 extract
abstract: We tested whether pollutant interaction signs remain fixed on every strictly increasing scale applied to reported arm means. A 2024 invertebrate extract gave 26 matched four-arm outcome sets. Eighteen positive and four negative signs were fixed on every scale. Four sets permitted both signs, although their raw and log signs agreed. These included both pollinator outcomes. Their minimum slope ratios for a zero contrast were 47.105 and 80.573. We provide exact bounds, a proof and finite sign witnesses. Independent order checks and 400 linear programs reproduced the results. These are fixed-mean scale diagnostics, not confidence intervals or biological effects. Shared facilities, selected outcomes, unverified extraction and unknown sampling covariance limit inference. Country and publication era could not support independent repeated tests. Climate responses were not tested. The package preserves code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, attribution and external regeneration instructions.

display.caption: Exact scale audit of fixed arm means. Twenty-two signs persist on all increasing scales. Four permit either sign. Counts are outcomes, not independent experiments. The slope ratio bounds the secant slopes across each outcome range.

citations.reason: Extends its raw and log scale audit to all increasing scales; records overlap.
Rebuilds its 26 matched sets from source; adds exact scale invariance and slope bounds.
Prior matching audit informs scope and observation bias.
Prior missing-arm bounds inform the complete-arm rule.
